# wl sync blocked: inbound worklog commits authored sorra@thewizardscode.com fail the author-identity gate

## Problem statement

`wl sync` in the SorraAgents checkout refuses to merge inbound worklog data when the incoming commits are authored by `sorra@thewizardscode.com` — a genuine project work identity used by the operator's other checkouts — because the author-identity gate accepted only the configured `user.email` (the GitHub noreply identity) plus the earlier `pi@local` exception. Work items and comments written from a `sorra@` checkout therefore stranded on the remote, and local work could not be published either (`wl sync --no-push` failed at the same pull/merge step).

## Users

- **Producer/operator (uses multiple checkouts).** "As the operator, I want worklog changes made from my `sorra@thewizardscode.com` checkout to merge on every agent host, so I do not have to re-author or hand-replay history per batch."
- **Agent sessions (Map, plan, audit).** "As an agent, I want `wl sync` to complete without `--allow-foreign-author`, so intake/plan/audit work is published instead of being stranded behind a gate refusal."

## Acceptance Criteria

- `wl sync` completes in the SorraAgents checkout (pull, merge and push) for inbound commits authored by `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, with no `--allow-foreign-author` override.
- The chosen policy is recorded in `syncAllowedAuthors` (`.worklog/config.yaml`) with a rationale comment, and the allow-list stays exact-email: no wildcards, no allow-all, empty author email still refused.
- The gate still refuses incident sentinel identities (`t@t.com` and the other `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS`), and no sentinel is ever added to the allow-list.
- Testing/validation: `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` passes and continues to pin exact-email semantics, empty-email refusal and sentinel refusal.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Policy-only fix: the gate decision logic is unchanged, so the existing regression contract (`tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py`) remains authoritative.
- The allow-list may not be widened beyond an explicit email list — no wildcard, no allow-all, and the empty-author-email refusal is never bypassed.
- Work is pushed to `dev` only (`main` is promoted by the ship skill).

## Existing state (verified during intake, 2026-11-04)

- `.worklog/config.yaml` → `syncAllowedAuthors` contains `250240+SorraTheOrc@users.noreply.github.com`, `pi@local` and `sorra@thewizardscode.com`, with a comment recording that the last entry is the project's own work identity, not a sentinel (`4e1ec2b6f`, present on `dev` and `main`).
- `scripts/check_git_identity.py` gate logic unchanged; `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` untouched.
- `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` drives the real exported `checkAuthorIdentity` gate and pins: `pi@local` accepted only via the allow-list, arbitrary foreign email refused, empty email refused even with `allowForeignAuthor`, sentinels never allow-listed. It reads the real project config, so the added entry participates in its membership/exactness assertions; the entry is not individually pinned by name.
- Verification this session: `wl sync --no-push` merged the inbound worklog data with no author-identity refusal (57 work items updated, 0 comments added, 0 `--allow-foreign-author` usage), so the four previously refused commits (`14e4cc89e`, `273325c35`, `23c315392`, `e8c0011a7`) now merge.
- Recurrence pattern: the same identity was refused on 2026-10-27 and again on 2026-10-29/10-31 (recurrence comment `SA-C0MVWICFTW001KBWQ`).

## Desired change

`sorra@thewizardscode.com` is accepted permanently as a permitted worklog-sync author through the project allow-list, while the gate's exact-email, empty-email and sentinel guarantees stay intact and continue to be covered by the existing regression tests.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.worklog/config.yaml` — `syncAllowedAuthors` entry plus the rationale comment (landed in `4e1ec2b6f`)
- `scripts/check_git_identity.py` — gate entry point and allow-list contract metadata; decision logic unchanged
- `tests/test_author_gate_allowlist.py` — allow-list contract regression tests (exact-email, empty-email, sentinel refusal)
- `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` — gate rules and the allow-list remediation procedure

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** `sorra@thewizardscode.com` is a real project identity, not a leaked/sentinel identity — it is absent from `INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` and the producer explicitly chose to allow-list it rather than re-author history.
- **Risk (drift):** no test pins the individual `sorra@` entry; removing it would re-strand sync, but loudly (a gate refusal on the next sync), and the contract-level guarantees stay pinned — accepted.
- **Risk (scope):** further identities must each be a separately reviewed config change, not bundled into this item.
- **Risk (widening):** the allow-list is a project-wide policy widening; it stays bounded because matching is exact-email and empty emails are always refused.

## Related work

- SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W — previous occurrence; the considered-but-rejected alternative (re-author the inbound `t@t.com` commits).
- SA-0MVGSB63F00803HK — precedent: allow-listing `pi@local` with the same bounded, exact-email approach.
- SA-0MVB57M02008QPJS — original author-identity gate incident and allow-list remediation guidance.
- SA-0MSW9RF740016WC7 — batch blocked by empty emails / `ross@example.com`.
- SA-0MVK4F993008D9S2 — `t@t.com`-authored commits on `refs/worklog/data`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interview round was required: the seed description already contained the problem statement and ACs, and the open decision had been answered by the producer in the worklog record.

- Q: "How should the four inbound `sorra@thewizardscode.com` worklog commits be handled — (1) allow-list the identity, (2) re-author the commits to the configured GitHub identity, or (3) another machine/agent identity policy?" — Answer (producer, plan session `herdr-1793454596-4112787-24238`, 2026-10-31): option 1, add the identity to the allow-list. Source: worklog comment `SA-C0MVWIN02D006Y7YM`. Research: the rejected alternative (re-authoring, the SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W playbook) would fix this batch only and recur on the next push from a `sorra@` checkout.
- Q: "Is `sorra@thewizardscode.com` a genuine identity or an incident sentinel?" — Answer (agent research): genuine project work identity; it is not listed in `scripts/check_git_identity.py::INCIDENT_ERA_EMAILS` and the config comment records it as the project's own work identity. Evidence: `.worklog/config.yaml`, `scripts/check_git_identity.py`.
- OPEN QUESTION: none.

- **SA-0MVLJDS04002KI1W** – wl sync blocked again: inbound t@t.com-authored worklog commits fail the author-identity gate (completed)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: accept, acceptance, add, agent, allow (+69 more)

Operator worklog sync from checkouts using `sorra@thewizardscode.com` now completes without manual intervention or `--allow-foreign-author` overrides.

## Problem

`tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` (added in v0.1.25) builds a fixture release repo and drives `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` with a stubbed suite runner. Under a clean shell the module is green (verified: `run_tests.py --scope full --force` at tree a9b008ead → 5820 passed). Under the **pre-push hook** (i.e. any push to `dev`/`main`) the same three tests fail:

```
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestGreenGate::test_green_gate_invokes_full_scope_and_release_proceeds
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestRedGate::test_red_gate_blocks_release_before_pr
FAILED tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py::TestMissingRunnerFailClosed::test_missing_runner_fails_closed
FileNotFoundError: .../runner-marker.txt   (the stubbed runner was never invoked)
```

Root cause: git exports `GIT_DIR` (and the suite gate may export `GIT_INDEX_FILE`) into hook environments; the fixture repo's git commands then resolve against the *live* checkout instead of the fixture, so `merge-dev-to-main.sh` short-circuits and the suite gate never runs. This is the same class as SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX (node fixtures inheriting the finish gate's `GIT_INDEX_FILE`).

**Consequence:** the pre-push full-suite gate is red for every `dev` push, so `dev` cannot be synced with `main` after a release (hit during the 2026-11-02 v0.1.25 release; the sync required `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` with a separately verified green tree).

## Impact

Users can now push `dev` after a release without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1`, enabling automated `dev`→`main` promotion to complete without manual intervention.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/test_release_full_suite_gate.py` scrubs the ambient git environment (`shared.git_sandbox.fixture_git_env()` or equivalent) for both the fixture repo construction and the merge-script subprocess, so it passes when run from a git hook.
2. A regression test proves the module passes with `GIT_DIR` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE` set to the live repository.
3. `git push origin dev` (fast-forward) succeeds without `TEST_SCOPE_SKIP=1` after the fix.
4. Full suite green in both a clean shell and a hook-like environment.

## Related

- SA-0MVYS34QF000AWQX — same leak class for node fixtures.
- SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42 — audit/producer-review churn (unrelated, same release session).

# Standup more focused on user experience (re-homed from ContextHub)

> **Provenance:** re-homed from ContextHub epic WL-0MW397N0Z002AYWP per producer
> decision (Option A). The standup skill source of truth lives in this
> (SorraAgents) repository — `skill/standup/` — which `~/.pi/agent/skills`
> symlinks to. The ContextHub copy is closed as moved.


## Problem statement

The daily standup report is currently a dry, flat bullet list of work items
("things done" + technical summaries), which is hard to read aloud and does
not convey what the user gained from the work. The output should be grouped
into meaningful categories, with each completed item described as a
single sentence about its impact on the user experience — without work item
IDs.

## Users

- The operator, who reads/listens to the daily standup (TTS) and wants a
  readable narrative of what changed and why it matters to the user.
- Agent sessions that generate standups and need clear, stable instructions
  for turning the script's structured data into the grouped report.

Example user stories:
- "As the operator, I want the standup grouped by areas such as 'User
  experience when doing Foo' and 'Back end stability under heavy load', so I
  can quickly grasp where progress happened and what each change means for
  users."
- "As the operator, I want each completed item described as one
  user-experience impact sentence without IDs, e.g. 'Improved the speed of
  user interactions with Foo by providing a one-click setup of the deck'."

## Desired change

1. **Categories** are chosen by the LLM (the invoking agent) at report time;
   labels are free-form (e.g. "User experience when doing Foo", "UI layout to
   improve access to key information"). No fixed taxonomy.
2. **Per-item impact sentences** come from a new explicit `## Impact` line in
   the work item description, written by the agent completing the work. Items
   without one (including all existing legacy items, which are **not**
   retrofitted) fall back to the current `Title — user story` phrasing.
3. **Grouped-paragraph format in every section** — "Yesterday I completed work
   on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus items for today",
   "Regressions" and "Blockers" — each section grouped **independently**
   (categories are chosen per section, not per whole report).
4. The deterministic script (`generate_standup.py`) continues to fetch and
   compute the selection data; it also extracts each item's `## Impact`
   sentence into the structured output. The LLM (agent session) does the
   clustering and paragraph rendering, keeping the script testable and the
   agent output interpretable.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `generate_standup.py` extracts the `## Impact` sentence from each item's
   description into a dedicated structured field (e.g. `impact`), available in
   `--json` output; a missing/malformed Impact section yields an empty field
   without error.
2. The rendered report is readable as a narrative: it organises each section's
   items into categories chosen by the LLM at report time, items are grouped
   **independently within each section**, and no work item IDs appear anywhere
   in the rendered report.
3. Within each category, every item is described as a single
   user-experience-focused sentence: the item's `## Impact` sentence when
   present, else the existing `Title — user story` phrasing (fallback).
4. The report remains first-person and TTS-friendly (spoken-form dates, no
   ID brackets/backticks/underscores in spoken lines) and stays within the
   ~2-minute read budget.
5. CLI behaviour is unchanged for consumers (flags, JSON schema superset,
   `--output-path` write path, sync-first, commit/push); existing tests keep
   passing with additions for the new `impact` extraction.
6. Work-item completion guidance (project AGENTS.md / implement skill / intake
   brief template) is updated so newly completed items carry an `## Impact`
   sentence describing the user-experience impact of the change.
7. Testing/validation: unit tests cover Impact extraction (present, absent,
   malformed) and the fallback; a golden-output test renders a sample report
   and asserts grouped sections, no IDs, and Impact-first sentences.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
   code comments, README, the standup SKILL.md, and any wiki/docs entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The script stays deterministic (no LLM calls inside `generate_standup.py`) —
  clustering/rendering happens in the invoking agent session per Q4 answer.
- Existing completed items are NOT retrofitted with `## Impact` lines.
- Report must stay first-person, TTS-friendly, under ~2 minutes reading time.
- No work item IDs in the rendered output.
- Surgical scope: the Herdr selection ordering and data sources are untouched.

## Existing state

- `skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` (installed to
  `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/`) renders a flat markdown report from the
  Herdr selection list; per-item text is `Title — user story/problem/summary`
  extracted heuristically from the description.
- Report structure: `## <project> Standup Report (date)` with sections
  "Yesterday I completed work on…", "Open critical items", "Additional focus
  items for today", "Regressions", "Blockers".
- Items already carry `Key Files` and (mostly) `As a …` user stories in their
  descriptions; there is no standard Impact field today.

## Desired change (implementation sketch)

- `generate_standup.py`: add `extract_impact(description)` (parse the
  `## Impact` section) and include `impact` in `normalize_item`/report data;
  keep `format_report` as a stable fallback for `--json` consumers and tests.
- `skill/standup/SKILL.md`: replace the "Report Structure" template with
  agent-rendered instructions: cluster each section's items into free-form
  categories, render one paragraph per category (one impact sentence per
  item), never render IDs, keep the TTS/first-person rules, note the
  `## Impact` / fallback rule.
- Work-item authoring guidance: add `## Impact` (one sentence,
  user-experience impact) to the completion conventions (implement skill
  output / AGENTS.md), so future standups have real impact sentences.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/SKILL.md` — report template → clustered paragraph
  rendering instructions; source of truth `skill/standup/SKILL.md` in the
  SorraAgents repo.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — add `## Impact`
  extraction + `impact` structured field; keep JSON/fallback compat.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_*.py` — new tests for
  Impact extraction, fallback, no-ID golden output.
- `AGENTS.md` (project + `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` global) / intake brief
  template — completed items gain an `## Impact` sentence.

## Related work

- **Create a podcast for standups (WL-0MVYZ458V004GRF8)** — consumes the
  rendered standup report; ensuring the grouped narrative stays parseable/TTS-
  friendly matters for it.
- Completed standup infra (sync-first WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K, maintenance
  routines WL-0MVIDWJ090090J3Q, scheduled prompts WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR) —
  unchanged; this is an output-format change.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: existing items are not retrofitted with Impact lines (fallback
  covers them). Confirmed by operator (Q5/A).
- Assumption: LLM clustering runs in the invoking agent session, not in the
  script (Q4/A). Risk: agent non-determinism → mitigations: keep deterministic
  data layer, document expected structure, golden output reviewed in tests at
  the data layer, SKILL.md instructions constrain clustering.
- Risk: paragraphs lengthen the report past 2 minutes → mitigation: the agent
  is instructed to keep each category paragraph tight and cap per-item
  sentences at one.
- Risk: Impact lines may be missing or low-quality → fallback + guidance
  update (AC6); scope-creep risk noted: no changes to Herdr selection or
  podcast pipeline (linked as related work, not scope).
- Risk: agents may accidentally include IDs → explicit "no IDs" rule in
  SKILL.md + golden-output test asserting absence (AC2).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "How should categories be determined?" — Answer (operator): "C — LLM-chosen at report time (free-form labels)". Source: interactive reply (round 1, 2026-11-06).
- Q2: "Where does each item's impact sentence come from?" — Answer (operator): "A — explicit `## Impact` line written into work items at completion; the script reads it". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "Which sections get the new grouped-paragraph format?" — Answer (operator): "C — every section, but group independently within the sections". Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q4: "Where does the LLM clustering run?" — Answer (operator): "A — in the invoking agent session; script emits structured item data; SKILL.md instructs the agent to cluster and render". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Q5: "Items without an `## Impact` line?" — Answer (operator): "A — fall back to current Title — user story phrasing". Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Assumption (confirmed implicitly): existing completed items are not retrofitted with Impact lines.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRMG8P2X004V6YC** – help line for chord commands too verbose (completed)

**73 open audit-side items** of the form `ruff <RULE> in <path> — candidate false positive` (`audit_runner.py` `FP_CANDIDATE_ANNOTATION`, created as "producer decision required" chores): **0 of 19 (path, rule) groups still fire** on the current tree.

Concrete examples of no-longer-reproducing findings that remained open:
- `S112` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — 22 items, 0 hits now.
- `SIM117` in `skill/implement/tests/test_implement_push_from_worktree.py` — 10 items, 0 hits now.
- `ISC004` in `tests/test_assignee_release_all_skills.py` — 7 items, 0 hits now.
- `PYI034`/`PYI036` in `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — 4 items, 0 hits now (these were orphaned children too).

Some of these block audits rather than sitting idle, so stale findings are not merely noise: `SA-0MVZNECSD005XB42` records the audit-side variant where every medium/low candidate-false-positive chore sets `needsProducerReview` and blocks closure.

## Why it matters

Stale items are indistinguishable from live work in every view. `wl next` will dispatch them, an agent will implement, and the audit skill must then decide whether a finding that no longer reproduces has been "fixed". The backlog reads as 444 actionable items when a large share are already resolved.

## Required behaviour (acceptance criteria)

1. Every linter-derived item records, at creation, the **exact verification command** and a **content fingerprint** (file hash + rule set) that produced it.
2. A re-verification sweep re-runs that command and, per item, classifies it as `still-reproduces`, `no-longer-reproduces` or `target-gone`, recording the evidence in a comment.
3. Items classified `target-gone` are closed with a rationale (or flagged for deletion), and items classified `no-longer-reproduces` are closed with the evidence comment — **never silently**.
4. The sweep is **dry-run by default** and only ever touches items it can attribute to a linter family (`Refactor` tag, `[SEVERITY] <path>` titles, `ruff <RULE> in <path>` titles). It must never close a human-authored bug or feature.
5. The sweep is runnable both ad hoc and as a scheduled/gated step (e.g. from the refactor skill or a `wl doctor`-style hook), and is idempotent.
6. Tests: target deleted → `target-gone`; diagnostic fixed → `no-longer-reproduces`; diagnostic still firing → untouched; human-authored item → never touched; dry-run makes no writes.

## Scope note

The sweep itself belongs in this repository (`skill/refactor/`, and the audit side in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`). If a worklog-level hook is preferred, that part belongs to the Worklog CLI project (`WL → /home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`) and should be raised there — recorded as an assumption, not a decision.

## Key Files

- `skill/refactor/workitem_creation.py` — record the verification command and content fingerprint (file hash + rule set) on every linter-derived item at creation (AC1).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — record the same metadata for audit-side candidate-false-positive chores (`FP_CANDIDATE_ANNOTATION` creations); note the existing `CFP-Chore-Key:` marker is reused as a stable key in the sweep's attribution logic.
- `skill/refactor/scripts/reverify.py` (new) — the dry-run-by-default re-verification sweep: classify `Refactor`-tagged, `[SEVERITY] <path>`/`ruff <RULE> in <path>` items as `still-reproduces` / `no-longer-reproduces` / `target-gone`, comment evidence, close with rationale (AC2–AC5).
- `skill/refactor/tests/` + `skill/audit/tests/` — coverage for AC6 scenarios (target deleted, diagnostic fixed, still firing, human-authored untouched, dry-run no-writes).

## Impact

Stale, already-fixed findings stop inflating the backlog and stop being dispatched to agents, so the queue can be trusted to mean "work that still needs doing".

# Audit integration worktree does not populate git submodules, causing false-negative build verdicts

## Problem statement

The audit's merge-gate integration step (`_integrate_into_dev`) creates a fresh
detached worktree at `origin/dev` with `git worktree add --detach` and runs
`npm run build` inside it. `git worktree add` never populates tracked
submodules, so any repository that vendors a submodule builds against an
**empty** submodule directory. The build fails with a module-resolution error,
execution-dependent ACs (e.g. "Build and full test suite pass") are marked
`partial`, and the item's verdict becomes "Ready to close: No" — a false
negative on a tree that builds green in the real, populated checkout.

## Users

- **Audit consumers (producers, implement agents)** — need an audit verdict
  that reflects the real tree; today a submodule-vendoring repo is
  systematically misjudged.
  - *As a producer, I want the audit's build verdict to reflect the populated
    checkout, so a green item isn't blocked by an environmental build failure.*
  - *As a ship/release operator, I want releases not to stall on a
    false-negative "not ready to close" caused by empty submodules.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- The integration worktree created by `_integrate_into_dev` has its tracked submodules populated **before** the build runs, so a repo with a submodule dependency has a non-empty submodule directory in that worktree.
- A build run in the integration worktree succeeds on a tree that builds green in the main checkout, so execution-dependent ACs are not marked `partial` for the empty-submodule reason.
- A repository without submodules is unaffected (fail-open), and a submodule-init failure logs a warning without aborting the audit.
- A regression test covers the submodule-population step in the integration worktree (uses the existing tracked-submodule fixture; red before the fix, green after).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Audits of build-dependent items on any submodule-vendoring repository reflect
the real tree, and releases stop being blocked by false-negative "not ready to
close" verdicts.

## Constraints

- **Fail-open is mandatory.** A repo without `.gitmodules` and any submodule-init
  failure must never abort or fail the audit — the worktree is then no worse
  than the launch checkout.
- **Do not re-implement the logic.** The audit runner already has
  `_ensure_execution_worktree_submodules` (added for the F3 execution worktree,
  SA-0MW4ZRLSI005PHL6), which mirrors `implement.py::_ensure_submodules`
  (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ). Reuse it (or promote it to a shared helper) rather
  than adding a third copy.
- **Ordering hazard (SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ):** submodule init must run *before*
  the `node_modules` symlink step in the worktree.
- Prefer the `git -c protocol.file.allow=always submodule update --init
  --recursive` invocation the existing audit helper uses (git ≥ 2.38 blocks the
  `file` transport by default, which breaks local-path submodules).
- Never `npm install` inside a worktree — the shared `node_modules` symlink
  convention (SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B) stands.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** the integration worktree is the only remaining audit worktree
  that runs a build/test against un-populated submodules (the execution
  worktree is already covered). Verified by grep; if a third worktree appears
  later it must apply the same helper.
- **Risk:** submodule init can be slow (large recursive trees) on the merge-gate
  critical path. Mitigation: keep the existing 600 s timeout and fail-open so a
  slow/failed fetch degrades to the old behaviour rather than blocking.
- **Risk:** network-dependent submodules can fail offline. Mitigation:
  fail-open with a warning in the integration evidence — never abort the audit.
- **Scope creep:** a build being green in *this* framework repo does not prove
  the tce-the-rising scenario; the regression test must use a tracked local-path
  submodule fixture, not a network clone. Other submodule-adjacent waxes (e.g.
  derived-file pin restoration) are separate items, already filed.

## Existing state

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_integrate_into_dev` (≈ line 11924)
  creates `audit-merge-<id>` with `git worktree add --detach`, symlinks
  `node_modules`, runs `npm run build`, then the suite, then pushes to `dev`.
  It contains **no** `git submodule update --init` call.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_ensure_execution_worktree_submodules`
  (≈ line 12149) already implements the exact fail-open behaviour for the
  **execution** worktree (`audit-exec-<id>`), including the `file`-protocol
  allowance and git-env scrubbing.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py::_ensure_submodules` (≈ line 7150)
  is the precedent helper for implement worktrees (SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_contaminated_launch.py` has a
  tracked-submodule fixture (`build_contaminated_launch_scenario` →
  `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/contaminated_launch.py`) used to prove the
  execution worktree submodule population.

## Desired change

In `_integrate_into_dev`, after the worktree is created and before the build,
populate tracked submodules using the existing audit helper (rename/generalise
`_ensure_execution_worktree_submodules` to a shared `_ensure_worktree_submodules`
if that reads cleaner). Append the outcome to the integration evidence. Cover
the new step with a regression test in the audit test suite.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — call the submodule-population helper from `_integrate_into_dev` before the build step; possibly generalise the existing helper name.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py` — add the integration-worktree submodule regression test.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_contaminated_launch.py` / `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/contaminated_launch.py` — reusable tracked-submodule fixture (reuse or extend).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — document the integration-worktree
  submodule population alongside the existing execution-worktree note (AC5).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — precedent `_ensure_submodules` (reference only, not modified).

## Related work

- **SA-0MW4ZRLSI005PHL6** (completed) — audit runs its pipeline in a fresh
  `origin/dev` worktree; added `_ensure_execution_worktree_submodules` for the
  *execution* worktree. This item closes the sibling gap in the *integration*
  worktree.
- **SA-0MWC6JJBR0050PGQ** (completed) — F3 suite executes in the fresh
  `origin/dev` worktree.
- **SA-0MSN52GGN002B0AZ** (completed) — `_ensure_submodules` for implement
  worktrees (the precedent).
- **SA-0MVTOR53E003IIEQ** — submodule-before-node_modules ordering hazard.
- **SA-0MSGS763C006SM1B** — worktree `node_modules` symlink convention.
- **RISE-0MW7YP6SD0091MKJ** (tce-the-rising) — per-project item superseded by
  this generic framework item (to be deleted).
- **SA-0MT456M27001LRTL** — merge gate / `verifyIntegration` origin.

### Related work (automated report)

- **SA-0MW6LOXBO0008706** – Ship release derived-files step must restore a build-rewritten submodule pin alongside the restored gitlink (completed)
- **SA-0MW06FLFR009F0P4** – Finish gate: report a lagging engine pin when the build fails after engine:sync (completed)
- **SA-0MVB71260006J3FY** – Migrate implement.py repo/worktree fixtures to git_sandbox (blocked)

#### Repository file matches

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`

## Evidence (preserved from seed)

- 2026-11-08 `tce-the-rising` audit of `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` AC4: build
  failed (exit 2) on missing vite config modules, not on the item's changes.
  The real populated tree builds green (`npm run build` exits 0) and the
  cached full suite is green.
- `vite.config.ts` imports from `./core/scripts/…`; `core/` is a tracked
  submodule. `git -c submodule.recurse=true worktree add --detach` leaves
  `core/` with 0 entries (git 2.53.0).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed context (problem statement,
precedent, evidence, and four draft ACs) was complete enough to draft this
brief. Gaps filled by research rather than interview:

- Q: *Which helper should the fix reuse?* — Answer (research): the audit
  runner already has `_ensure_execution_worktree_submodules`
  (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` ≈ line 12149) implementing the exact
  fail-open, `file`-protocol-allowed `git submodule update --init --recursive`
  pattern; reuse/generalise it rather than copying `implement.py::_ensure_submodules`.
  Source: `grep` of `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`.
- Q: *Is there an existing tracked-submodule test fixture?* — Answer
  (research): yes — `skill/audit/tests/fixtures/contaminated_launch.py` builds
  a scenario with a `core/` submodule; the regression test can reuse/extend it.
  Source: `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_contaminated_launch.py`.

# Audit runner leaves items at open/plan_complete after a failing/aborted audit when a concurrent wl sync races its restore (lost update)

## Problem statement

During an audit, `audit_runner.py` transitions the target item out of
`completed`/`in_review` (to `in-progress`/`in_review` or `open`/`plan_complete`)
and is supposed to **restore it to `completed`/`in_review`** on every exit path
(the abort path logs `Aborted audit for <id>: restoring "completed" "in_review"`).

Under concurrency this restore is **lost**: a `wl sync` running in another
session (or the audit runner's own sync) races the restore, and the item is
left stuck at `open`/`plan_complete` (status `open`, stage `plan_complete`,
`auditResult: null`). The item silently drops out of the release candidate set
(`stage: in_review`) and looks like brand-new, un-implemented work — a
**worklog data-integrity regression**, not a cosmetic glitch.

This is the same class as the known concurrent-`wl sync` lost-update race
(WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ); the audit runner's own status restore is not
race-safe against it.

## Users

- **Release operators** running `/skill:ship release` — corrupted items silently
  drop out of the release candidate set, causing releases to omit valid items or
  include items that failed audit.
- **Agents** implementing work — an item left at `open`/`plan_complete` looks
  like un-implemented work and may be picked up for re-implementation.
- **Producer reviewers** — corrupted items appear in the wrong state in the
  worklog dashboard and reports.

## Observed (2026-11-08, tce-the-rising `/skill:ship release`)

A single release attempt corrupted **four** items, each left at
`open`/`plan_complete` although all four were `completed`/`in_review` before:

| Item | Corrupted by | Prior state (from worklog-data history) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `RISE-0MVWWBT8Y009FMZ6` | release gate audit remediation (14:00) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MW3MXVU5009GMLR` | `--refresh-audits` (14:38) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MVXSNH71005PONU` | `audit_runner.py issue` (14:57) | `completed`/`in_review` |
| `RISE-0MW3GUQKX004W74K` | `audit_runner.py issue` (14:59) | `completed`/`in_review` |

All four were repaired by hand (`wl update <id> --status completed --stage
in_review`) after reconstructing the prior state from the `refs/worklog/...`
delta history. The corruption spans both the failing-verdict path (a
persisted "Ready to close: No" still left the item at `open`/`plan_complete`)
and the aborted path (the "restoring" message logged but the restore did not
persist).

## Root-cause hypotheses to confirm

- The restore is a plain `wl update` with no compare-and-swap / version guard,
  so a concurrent `wl sync` (pull→merge→push) overwrites it (last-writer-wins
  on a stale snapshot).
- A failing/aborted audit may not run the restore at all on some exit paths
  (the observed `open`/`plan_complete` with a persisted failing verdict
  suggests the restore is skipped when the verdict is not "Yes").

## Desired change

Make the audit runner's status restore **race-safe and unconditional**:

- Restore `completed`/`in_review` on **every** exit path — success, failing
  verdict, abort, exception, timeout — via `try/finally`.
- Use the shared `StatusLifecycle` helper (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`)
  and its claim/assignee handling so the restore participates in the same
  lost-update protection as other lifecycle exits.
- Guard the restore against a concurrent `wl sync` (e.g. re-read after write,
  retry on mismatch — the same verification pattern the ship skill uses for
  close verification, SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- Never leave an item at `open`/`plan_complete` merely because an audit failed
  — a failing verdict is recorded while the item stays `completed`/`in_review`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An explicit `Ready to close: No` verdict demotes the item to `open`/`plan_complete` deliberately and verified (this is the audit-reject contract); an infra-fallback-tainted, aborted, timed-out or crashed audit never demotes.
- [ ] An aborted audit restores the item to `completed`/`in_review`, verified after write and retried once if a concurrent `wl sync` clobbered the restore.
- [ ] The restore runs on every exit path via `try/finally`, including exceptions raised after the `in_progress` claim.
- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` between the audit status change and its restore and asserts the item ends `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] No item is left at `open`/`plan_complete` or `in_progress` as a side effect of any audit path, and an unverified restore is never reported as success.

## Impact

Auditing an `in_review` item can no longer silently revert it to un-implemented
work, so release candidate sets and worklog state stay correct under
concurrent agent sessions.

## Constraints

- The audit runner's core auditing semantics (what gets audited, how verdicts
  are calculated) must not change — only the status-restore path is affected.
- The fix must not introduce additional contention on the worklog database
  that would slow down normal audit throughput.
- The restore must use the same `--worklog-dir` resolution as the rest of the
  audit runner (cwd-independent).

## Existing state

`audit_runner.py` transitions the target item to `open`/`plan_complete` at the
start of an audit and has restore logic on the abort path, but:
- The restore is not wrapped in `try/finally` (missing on some exit paths).
- The restore is a plain `wl update` — no re-read/verify/retry against concurrent
  `wl sync` (the same pattern fixed in SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- The failing-verdict path may skip the restore entirely.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Audit runner core; status transition and restore logic live here.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Shared lifecycle helper with claim/assignee semantics.
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — Reference for the close-verification retry pattern (SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5).
- `skill/audit/tests/` — Test directory for audit runner tests.
- `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` — The `wl sync` helper that the race originates from.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5** — Ship release must verify in-scope work items are actually closed before reporting success (lost-update close verification pattern).
- **SA-0MVE34D9B005TUYJ** — wl sync --if-idle reverts actively-worked items to open/intake_complete (lost-update race fix).
- **SA-0MVWFPI31000HP3H** — Only mark as complete when fully complete (adjacent lifecycle-transition safety).
- **SA-0MVI35BIU002MTZQ** — Audit runner: parent-persisted child audits demote in_review children (completed) (adjacent audit-raced-lifecycle-transition precedent).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The restore logic exists on the abort path but is lost to race — not completely absent. Needs code verification.
- **Risk:** Adding a retry loop to the restore could introduce subtle timing issues if the retry window overlaps with other concurrent operations.
- **Risk:** The fix must not change audit timing behaviour — agents must not see longer audit durations.
- **Scope creep:** Fixing the general `wl sync` lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ) is out of scope; this item only fixes the audit runner's restore path.


## Plan (plan skill, 2026-11-13)

Planning decision: **plan required** (effort Small / risk Medium — above the
auto-skip threshold). Approval gate not requested (only *Extra Large* effort
**and** *High/Severe* risk triggers an approval pause).

### Code inspection results (closes the two open questions in this item)

1. **"Has the failing-verdict path been verified to run the restore?"**
   Partly — and the reported symptom is (mostly) a misdiagnosis. A genuine
   explicit `Ready to close: No` verdict **deliberately demotes** to
   `open`/`plan_complete` (the audit-reject workflow: `_apply_terminal_lifecycle`
   'no' branch; documented in `skill/audit/SKILL.md` → Status Lifecycle;
   pinned by `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`
   `test_ready_no_sets_open_plan_complete` and `test_audit_runner_core.py`
   "A 'No' verdict still demotes to open/plan_complete"). An
   **infra-fallback-tainted** `No`, a timeout, a provider error, a parse
   failure or a crash takes the **restore** branch and must never demote.
   The observed `open`/`plan_complete` items all had `auditResult: null`,
   i.e. the run never persisted a verdict — consistent with an aborted run
   whose restore was lost, not with a demoting `No`.
2. **"Does `StatusLifecycle` provide verify-then-retry?"** No. The in-run
   lifecycle verification/retry (3 attempts, linear backoff) lives in
   `_apply_terminal_lifecycle` (WL-0MSVVFBJ2003RRYK), *not* in
   `StatusLifecycle`. Three restore paths are weaker or unverified:
   - `_restore_pre_audit_state_on_failure` — one write, one readback, no retry.
   - `_restore_work_item_status` (SIGTERM/SIGINT handler) — one write, **no
     readback**.
   - `check-audit-gate.js::checkAndRestoreStuckAudit` — the parent-side
     SIGKILL recovery that logs `Aborted audit for <id>: restoring ...`:
     a bare `wl update`, **no readback, no retry**, and the state file is
     deleted even when the restore did not persist (so a lost update is
     unrecoverable). This is the exact log line quoted in the problem
     statement. The same gap applies to every other state-file consumer.
   - `cmd_issue`'s `finally` is entered *after* the `in_progress` claim in
     `_phase_gate`, so an exception between the claim and the `try`
     (`audit_lease_begin`, `_open_checkpoint_store`) leaves the claim behind.
   - `wl audit-set --ready-to-close no` demotes as a *persist-time side
     effect* (worklog `revertToPlanComplete`), before the terminal
     lifecycle corrects it — an unguarded window on restore-bound runs
     (same class as SA-0MVI35BIU002MTZQ, fixed there for children only).

### Plan decision D1 — AC1 wording reconciled (producer confirmation requested)

AC1 as originally written ("a failing verdict leaves the item at
`completed`/`in_review` — never `open`/`plan_complete`") **contradicts the
documented, tested audit-reject contract** described above; implementing it
literally would remove the mechanism that returns rejected work to the
actionable queue, invalidate 8+ existing tests, and change release-gate
semantics. Evidence (source code and tests override the worklog text)
supports narrowing AC1 to: *an explicit `No` demotes deliberately and
verified; nothing else may demote, ever*. This is recorded as producer
question Q3 in the Appendix and the item carries `needsProducerReview`, so
the producer can overrule before the policy child is implemented. If
overruled, only child F4 (policy) and AC1 change — the three mechanical
fixes stand unchanged.

### Features (vertical slices, test-first order)

| # | Child | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F1 | Race-clobber restore regression tests | task | Deterministic clobber injection (tests first, red before the fix) |
| F2 | Verified-retry in-run lifecycle restore | task | Python runner: settle-verify-retry on every restore path + claim inside the guard |
| F3 | Verified-retry parent-side abort restore | task | `check-audit-gate.js` state-file restore: readback + one retry + retained state file |
| F4 | Verdict-demotion policy documented and pinned | docs | Document reconciled contract; pin explicit-`No` demotion vs never-demote paths |

Each child is a deliverable end-to-end slice (code + tests + docs where
applicable). No horizontal layer phases are needed at this size.

### Requirement to feature mapping

| Requirement (this item) | Covered by |
| --- | --- |
| Desired change 1 - restore on every exit path (`try/finally`, exceptions) | F2 (in-run, claim inside the guard), F3 (parent-side abort) |
| Desired change 2 - use the shared `StatusLifecycle` claim/assignee handling | F2 (key file + assignee-release semantics; reuse the shared claim-release predicate) |
| Desired change 3 - guard the restore against a concurrent `wl sync` (re-read/retry) | F1 (red test), F2, F3 |
| Desired change 4 - never leave an item `open`/`plan_complete` merely because an audit failed (reconciled by D1: only a genuine explicit `No` demotes) | F2, F4 |
| AC1 (reworded by D1) | F2 (non-demoting paths) + F4 (contract pinned; awaits Q3) |
| AC4 (regression test injecting a concurrent `wl sync`) | F1 |
| Constraints - semantics unchanged, no added contention, cwd-independent `--worklog-dir` | F2 (explicit ACs); F3 (state-file dirs unchanged) |

### Traceability

- Duplicate check performed (`wl search` "restore race lifecycle", `wl search`
  "audit restore lost update"): no full duplicate. Precedents:
  SA-0MRNKVPTA005FKBG (restore-pre-audit-state), SA-0MTRH8C5O005URGR (abort
  recovery state file), SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5 (close verification), and the
  partially overlapping open idea SA-0MVIO0WQW006Y1FS (audit slot + verdict
  lifecycle idempotence) — related, not duplicate.

## Objective

Make `/skill:ship release` judge the importance of the work items in the release and propose the semantically correct semver bump (patch, minor, or major), instead of always bumping patch — with the producer asked in the PI session before any non-patch bump is applied.

## Problem Statement

The ship skill currently always increments the `z` (patch) component of the release version (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` defaults `BUMP="patch"`), even when the release adds new or breaking capability. Releases that add features therefore ship as patch versions (e.g. `v0.1.19` instead of `v0.2.0`), misrepresenting the release's impact and forcing the producer to remember `--bump minor` manually.

## Users

- **Release manager (the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`)** — must judge the release's importance from the items being shipped and propose the right bump without extra flags.
- **Producer** — must see and approve any non-patch bump, in the session, with a full justification naming the items that triggered it.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when every item in the release is a fix, chore, or documentation change, I want the release to bump patch automatically so that I don't have to think about semver.
- As a release manager, when the release contains meaningful new capability, I want to propose a minor bump with evidence, rather than silently shipping it as a patch.
- As a producer, I want to be asked, in the session, before a minor or major bump is applied, with a justification naming the items and why they warrant the bump — and I want to be able to decline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- The agent judges the importance of the release from those items and proposes exactly one bump: **patch** when the release only fixes, documents, or maintains; **minor** when it adds meaningful new capability; **major** when it breaks or removes existing capability or otherwise changes behaviour incompatibly (the existing `--bump` override remains available).
- A **patch** proposal proceeds automatically with no producer interaction — the current `--bump patch` behaviour and `merge-dev-to-main.sh` default are unchanged.
- A **minor or major** proposal prints a full justification — each contributing item ID and title, why it warrants the bump, and the proposed `old → new` version — and the agent asks the producer **in the PI session**; no git mutation, tag, PR, or worklog close occurs until the producer approves.
- Producer approval proceeds with the approved `--bump`; a declined non-patch proposal is honoured (the agent does not apply it, and records the decision and the producer's preferred bump in the session and on the release's work item).
- In a non-interactive/headless context where the producer cannot be asked, a minor or major proposal is never auto-approved: the agent records the justification, flags the item for producer review, and stops.
- The judgement is based on the release items' content (Impact/description/capability), not on `issueType` or a label lookup; the justification cites the evidence used.
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics rather than duplicating version arithmetic.
- Unit tests cover: candidate gathering (including an empty candidate set), the review packet/justification rendering, patch auto-proceed, and the non-patch approval-pending behaviour (no mutation); no test reads or mutates the live worklog.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, and code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Releases that add or break capability will carry a version number that reflects it, and producers will be asked in-session to approve that call with evidence instead of policing `--bump` flags by hand.

## Existing State

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` sets `BUMP="patch"` by default and accepts `--bump patch|minor|major` (already validates the value).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` parses and forwards `--bump` to the merge script; the wrapper has no bump evaluation step and its documented exit codes are `0`–`14`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` already implements `patch`/`minor`/`major` arithmetic correctly (including `z = 0` on minor and `y = z = 0` on major) and resolves `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` as the version source.
- Release candidates are items with `stage: in_review` (`check-audit-gate.js::getCandidateItems`), so the candidate set already exists.
- The release wrapper subprocess is non-interactive, but the ship skill itself is a PI skill executed by an agent in a session — the agent, not the shell script, is the component that can ask the producer.

## Desired Change

1. Add a small, unit-testable helper (e.g. `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js`) that gathers release candidates and renders a compact review packet: per item `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, `## Impact` (or user story) and a truncated description excerpt, plus the current version and the three candidate bump outcomes. It gathers and renders only — no judgement, no mutation.
2. Add a "Version bump evaluation" step at the start of the documented release workflow in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (before gates and merge): run the preflight, judge the release's importance, and choose patch/minor/major.
3. Patch → run the release normally (patch is the existing default).
4. Minor/major → present the justification to the producer in the session and wait for approval; on approval run `run-release.js --bump <approved>`; on decline, do not apply.
5. Keep the judgement rationale and the producer's decision in the session output and, where the release is tied to a work item, in a comment so the version choice is auditable.
6. Update `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and the SKILL.md workflow/argument docs to describe the evaluation step and the in-session approval gate.

## Constraints

- **Judgement stays with the agent:** no issue-type or label mapping, and no mechanical classifier is added — the evaluation prompt/rubric is documented, and the agent makes the call from the items' content.
- **Producer gates non-patch bumps:** minor and major bumps must never be applied without an explicit producer approval in the session. Patch bumps stay automatic.
- **Fail-closed in headless runs:** where no producer is available (downtime/automated dispatches), a minor/major proposal must stop with producer review rather than self-approve.
- **Backward compatible:** an explicit `--bump` keeps its current meaning and precedence; invoking `merge-dev-to-main.sh` directly keeps its `patch` default.
- **No duplicated version arithmetic:** reuse `bump-version.js` for the actual bump; the new code only gathers evidence and renders the proposal.
- **Fail-safe:** an unreadable/empty candidate set must default to patch with a warning and must never block a release that would otherwise succeed; a preflight failure must not mutate the repository.
- **No live-worklog test access:** unit tests must inject the candidate-fetch boundary.
- **Auditability:** the proposed and approved bump, the justification, and the producer's decision are recorded (session output plus a work-item comment for item-linked releases).

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — new "Version bump evaluation" workflow step, in-session approval gate, argument/behaviour docs.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` — new candidate-gathering/review-packet helper (and its tests).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — unchanged `--bump` forwarding, plus any logging of the decided bump; verify no new git side effects.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — receives the decided `--bump`; default unchanged.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` — reused as-is for arithmetic (verify minor resets patch to `0`, major resets minor and patch).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getCandidateItems` is the release-candidate source.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — reference for the evaluation step and approval gate.
- `skill/ship/tests/` — new unit tests for the preflight helper and the approval-pending path.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** — Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (introduced the bump step and `v<semver>` tag convention).
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** — ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (version source resolution).
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** — Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs.
- **SA-0MQI6MDUP001S8NL** — bump-version.js isMainModule check fails on symlinked install paths.
- **SA-0MRGVN9XM003LNQ7** — Close work items when shipping (uses the released version in `Shipped in v<version>` markers).
- **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** — Newly-created-tag gate (precedent for a fail-closed startup gate with a distinct exit code).
- **SA-0MUIVIJFT0009ZNV** — Missing-script fail-fast (precedent for refusing early, before any git/worklog side effects).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Judgement subjectivity (risk):** "meaningful new capability" is a judgement call, and two agents could judge the same release differently. Mitigation: a documented rubric (new capability → minor, breaking change → major, fixes/docs/maintenance only → patch), the evidence-based justification, and the producer's in-session approval for every non-patch bump.
- **Producer availability (risk):** a headless release cannot ask anyone. Mitigation: a non-patch proposal in a headless run stops with producer review instead of self-approving; patch releases are unaffected.
- **Agent discipline (risk):** the gate lives in the documented workflow, so a release run by bypassing the skill (direct `run-release.js`) is not gated. Mitigation: document the workflow as the canonical path, and keep the version arithmetic and safety gates in the script unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-item bump annotations, automatic CHANGELOG grouping, and mechanical classification are separate opportunities and should be filed as follow-up items rather than folded into this change.
- **Empty candidate set:** a release with no `in_review` items (e.g. hotfix) defaults to patch and logs why.
- **`--skip-checks` interaction (assumption):** `--skip-checks` bypasses branch/critical gates only; the bump evaluation still runs, and an explicit `--bump` remains an operator override.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (basis for minor-worthiness):** How should the release's importance be judged?
  - Options considered: (A) by `issueType`; (B) by `priority`; (C) by an explicit label/tag; (D) the agent's interpretation of the items' importance.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's not about issue type or label. It's about your interpretation of the importance of the items in the release. Make the best call you can. Check with the producer." → **Option D**, with a documented rubric and producer confirmation.
- **Q2 (approval mechanism):** How is the producer asked to approve a proposed minor/major bump?
  - Options considered: (A) fail-closed exit code + producer re-runs with `--bump`; (B) an interactive prompt inside the PI session; (C) automatic bump with a warning.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's a skill in PI, ask in the session." → **Option B**: the agent presents the justification and asks the producer in the session; the subprocess itself stays non-interactive.
- **Q3 (major inference):** Should a `major` (x) bump be inferred?
  - Options considered: (A) no — only minor/patch; (B) infer and suggest major, but never apply without producer approval.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "You can infer it and suggest it, but never implement without checking with the producer." → **Option B**: major may be proposed and justified, gated by the same in-session producer approval as minor.

# Slot-wait measurement harness counts a read of a fixture file as genuine runs (spurious 999.0 s sample)

Discovered-from: **SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU** (residual post-fix slot-wait re-measurement follow-up).

## Problem statement

The `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` harness's genuine-run filter admits tool results from non-bash tools (e.g. `read`) when their text contains structural markers, so fixture text echoed by a file read is parsed as genuine slot-wait measurements — producing a spurious 999.0 s sample that fails the `no_run_over_120s` threshold.

## Target outcome

Fix the `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` false positive so that reading a fixture/source file can never be counted as a genuine test-slot run, restoring a trustworthy `no_run_over_120s` verdict.

## Users

- **Producer / agent operators** running the slot-wait re-measurement harness to verify the 2026-10-31 fast-lane fix removed test-slot starvation. A false-positive breach invalidates their verdict and blocks RCA closure.
- Example user story: *As a producer closing the slot-starvation RCA (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV), I need the harness verdict to reflect only real runs, so that a `fail` genuinely means users are still waiting > 120 s for a slot.*

## Existing state (evidence, 2026-11-10)

Running `python3 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py --json` over the full window reports a spurious **999.0 s** `dev_push_gate` sample. It is an artefact, not a run:

- An agent `read` `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` (session record `2026-11-10T15:23:02.987Z`).
- That file contains the fixture text `"slot_wait_seconds": 999.0` plus a `run_tests: gate-subject` marker.
- The harness's genuine-run filter trusts a tool result whose text carries a structural marker when no bash command is resolvable. A `read` tool result has no bash command, so the fixture text is parsed as **four fake gate samples** (122.687, 9.0, 1.25, 999.0).
- Effect: `dev_push_gate` inflates from 5 calls / max 0.002 s to 9 calls / max 999.0 s, and `no_run_over_120s` fails on a non-existent run.

Reproduction (confirmed): `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import measure_slot_wait as m; print(m.parse_block(open('tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py').read())['gate'])"` — prints the four injected samples.

Root cause: `measure()` pairs each `toolResult` with its assistant `toolCall` command via `_commands_by_tool_call`, which maps **only `bash` tool calls**. A `read`/`edit`/`write`/`grep` result therefore resolves to `command=None` and falls through to the `_has_structural_marker` fallback intended for genuine bash runs whose call record is missing (forked/compacted logs).

## Desired change

Distinguish "no command resolvable because the log is incomplete" from "no command because the result came from a non-bash tool". The `toolResult` message itself carries `toolName`; only `bash` results (or a result with no tool name) may use the structural-marker fallback. A result whose `toolName` is a non-bash tool is never a measurement, regardless of its text.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `read` (or any non-bash tool) result that merely echoes fixture text is never counted as a genuine run sample.
2. A regression test proves reading `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` (and a generic fixture file) injects zero samples.
3. The genuine-run filter still accepts real run sources (`run_tests.py`, `implement.py`, `git push`, `wait_for_job.py`) and genuine structural-marker results with no resolvable command.
4. `python3 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py --json` over the full window no longer reports the 999.0 s sample.
5. Testing/validation criterion: the regression test fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The slot-wait re-measurement harness stops reporting phantom breaches, so the parent RCA's threshold verdict is trustworthy.

## Constraints

- Read-only measurement tooling; never synthesise load.
- No change to the lane ceilings or threshold values.

## Key Files

- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — genuine-run filter in `measure()`; also the module docstring's "Attribution — genuine run filter" section.
- `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` — regression test for the fixture-echo false positive.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — "Genuine-run filter" paragraph (needs the bash-only rule stated).

## Related work

- `SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU` — the follow-up item whose re-measurement surfaced this artefact.
- `SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K` — the harness's originating item.
- `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` — parent; its AC3 threshold check is the consumer of this verdict.
- `SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI` — ruff ISC004 flagging `measure_slot_wait.py`; same file, unrelated lint false-positive, do not conflate with this fix.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the fix must not tighten acceptance for valid cases — genuine structural-marker results from bash runs with missing call records must still pass.
- **Confirmed assumption**: `toolResult` messages carry a `toolName` field set to `"bash"` on genuine bash tool results. Verified across a ~3,000-result sample of `~/.pi/agent/sessions`: `bash` 2346, `read` 394, `edit` 251, `write` 56, `grep` 17, `skill_path` 1 — every genuine run source is `bash`, so a `toolName != "bash"` guard is safe.
- **Assumption**: no non-bash tool legitimately carries slot-wait data in its result text.
- **Scope-creep risk**: do not extend the fix to other measurement harnesses (`measure_audit_performance.py`) unless they exhibit the same pattern.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions asked — the work item description provides sufficient evidence, reproduction steps, and acceptance criteria to proceed. Verified independently: (a) the reproduction prints the four injected gate samples; (b) `toolName` is present and `bash`-only for genuine runs across the session corpus; (c) the "Genuine-run filter" docs paragraph is the only prose describing the fallback.

# Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound

## Goal (user story)

As a producer running a release (`/skill:ship release`) on a contended host, I want the release
gate to distinguish "the suite is red" from "the host is busy", so a busy machine can no longer
fail a green release with a 300 s hang timeout. The unit stage, not a browser loop, was the abort
point this time — the diagnostic currently explains only browser-stage hangs and conflates elapsed
time with the bound.

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The dev→main release gate aborted the TCE v0.1.24 release with
`[hang-timeout] Vitest run did not complete within 300s — aborting (exit 124)` +
`[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=124 outcome=hang args="--project unit" expected=241 ran=indeterminate`.
No test failed — the unit stage was still working through 241 files under host load (three
concurrent suite runs + a Monte-Carlo sweep; 16 cores, load average reported 35–42). A retry cost
a full 20+ minute re-run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `[hang-timeout]` abort reports, in the same message: the aborted stage (
  `--project unit` / `--project browser` / the pre-flight `vitest list`), the configured bound,
  the elapsed wall time, the delta over the bound, and the host load average at abort plus the
  core count — so contention is distinguishable from a genuine hang without opening the cache entry.
- The hang diagnostic's guidance is stage-appropriate: the browser-stage paragraph (starved
  `requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under `--project browser`) is
  **not** printed for a unit-stage abort, which instead points at a synchronous loop in
  test/engine code.
- The unit-stage wall-clock bound adopts the operator-approved **hybrid** strategy: a raised
  **static floor** (justified against the measured baseline — TCE green unit stages observed at
  88–217 s against the current 300 s bound, i.e. ~1.4× headroom) **plus load-aware scaling** of the
  bound from the sampled 1-min load average relative to the core count, **up to a finite ceiling**;
  the bound remains overridable per host (`--timeout-ms`).
- The hybrid bound's rationale and the measured baseline are recorded in the runner/CI header
  comment(s) and in the release-gate documentation (this repo's `docs/`, and TCE's
  `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` header + `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout).
- Inner stage bounds stay consistent with the outer gate budget: the sum of stage bounds cannot
  silently exceed the outer per-command timeout (TCE `.pi/test-config.json` →
  `timeoutPerCommand: 1500`, for an 18–21 min suite — ~4–7 min headroom), so raising/scaling an
  inner bound either adjusts the outer budget in the same change or documents why it still fits.
- Hang semantics are unchanged: exit `124` (`HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`), hangs are **never
  retried**, and the `--expect-project-coverage` gate still fails closed on an incomplete run.
- Tests cover the new diagnostic content (stage, bound, elapsed, delta, load average) and the
  bound/load behaviour deterministically: the load average is injected through a test seam and is
  never read from the real host.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A producer can retry a release on a busy machine and see immediately whether the suite or the host
was at fault, instead of losing a full-suite run to a timeout that had nothing to do with the code.

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken hang detection.** Exit 124, "hangs are never retried" and the fail-closed
  coverage gate are invariants (TCE precedent CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N, CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H); a bound
  that never fires is a regression in the opposite direction — keep the ceiling finite and print
  the bound in the diagnostic so an operator can see how generous it was.
- **Portability.** The bound must remain an explicit, per-host tunable; a load-aware bound is an
  addition, not a replacement for an overridable number, and smaller CI hosts still get a sane
  floor.
- **Determinism in tests.** Never read the real load average in a test; sample it behind an
  injectable seam.
- **Cross-repo tracking.** This item owns the work; TCE-side files below are edited in the TCE
  checkout (per the cross-repo convention) and recorded on this item. The release gate itself
  lives in `skill/ship/` in this repo.
- **Scope discipline.** A fully load-aware *outer* gate timeout and per-file retry budgets are out
  of scope; record them as linked work items rather than folding them in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- This repo (framework): `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (outer per-command timeout budgeting,
  any stage-bound surface), `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` (gate log surface),
  release-gate docs in `docs/`.
- Cross-repo (TCE checkout; tracked here): `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` (hang diagnostic
  content, load-average sampling seam, hybrid bound derivation), `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  (unit-stage `--timeout-ms 300000`, header comment rationale),
  `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` (diagnostic + bound coverage with injected load),
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (hang-timeout section ~line 1313, test-config section ~line 816),
  `.pi/test-config.json` (`timeoutPerCommand: 1500` if the outer budget is adjusted).

## Design decision for the plan (not blocking intake)

The hybrid bound may be implemented **in place** in TCE's `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` with
this item tracking the change, or the bounded runner may be **lifted into the framework**
(e.g. under `skill/test/scripts/`) and consumed by TCE. Both satisfy the ACs; the plan decides and
records the choice, keeping the diagnostic and bound computation in exactly one place.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N** (TCE, completed) — introduced the bounded wall-clock abort, exit 124,
  the never-retry rule, and raised the browser bound 15→20 min after variance straddled the old
  limit; this item is the same failure mode one stage earlier.
- **CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H** (TCE, completed) — the project-coverage gate whose fail-closed behaviour
  must be preserved.
- **CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09** (TCE, superseded/deleted) — the original intake that produced this
  brief; measured evidence and the evidence corrections (retry log shows a producer-review block,
  not a green retry; load 35–42 is an observation, not a log) carry over.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** (this repo) — the full-suite-at-dev-push gate design this work hardens.

# Release gate: preserve green full-suite cache entries so a unit-stage hang abort resumes

## Goal (user story)

As a producer running a release, I want a unit-stage hang abort to **not** force a full 20+ minute
re-run when the tree is unchanged: the gate should resume from a green cached full-suite entry
within the cache TTL instead of re-executing the whole suite.

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The TCE v0.1.24 release gate aborted in the unit stage with a 300 s hang bound (exit 124; no
failing test — host contention, load 35–42 on 16 cores). The per-repo test cache is keyed on
command + git state with a 2 h TTL; the hang **overwrites** the cache entry for that state with
`exit_code: 124`, so a retry on the same tree re-runs every stage from scratch. The release gate
runs `python3 run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` on the merged dev→main tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hang/abort result (exit `124` from the bounded vitest runner, or any non-zero abort that
  produced no parsable test results) does **not** destroy a green cache entry for the same tree
  state: when a valid green entry exists for the requested command+state within TTL, the cached
  green verdict is served even if a later aborted run wrote to the same key, and the abort is
  still reported (the gate must never *silently* accept an abort as green).
- The resume path is functional end-to-end: re-running the release gate against an unchanged tree
  (same git state, within TTL) after a unit-stage abort consumes the preserved green full-suite
  entry instead of re-executing `npm --silent test`, with the cache TTL gate intact.
- The release gate documents the resume procedure: `run_tests.py`/cache behaviour and the
  operator-visible statement ("the tree is unchanged within TTL — re-run resumes green") are
  described in this repo's release-gate docs and in `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
  comments; no green-entry destruction happens on abort.
- A failure or changed tree still executes and stores freshly — the preservation never masks a red
  run, a changed git state, or an expired TTL: cache behaviour for abort entries is covered by
  tests in this repo (`tests/` alongside `test_cache.py` / `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A contended-host abort stops costing a full re-run: the producer retries the release and the gate
resumes from the green entry for the unchanged tree, holding the green verdict while the abort is
still surfaced.

## Constraints

- **Never mask a genuine failure.** A preserved green entry is served only for the same command +
  git state within TTL; any tree change, red verdict, or TTL expiry forces a fresh run.
- **Green-first, but loud.** Returning the preserved green entry must be paired with a clear
  notice that the *aborted* run is being satisfied from the earlier green entry (operator
  visibility), not a silent acceptance of exit 124.
- **Follow the existing cache contract.** Keying, git-state fingerprinting, `scope` / `test_type`
  namespacing and the state-changed quarantine in `test_cache.py` are unchanged; this item only
  refines what a hang/abort writes.
- **Cross-repo consumers.** TCE's audit/release flows consume `query_cached()`; their
  expectations (read-only, verdicts only for matching state) must not regress.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `test_cache.py` (this repo root) — store/lookup semantics for hang/abort (exit 124) entries;
  green-entry preservation; TTL unchanged.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `run_cached`/`query_cached` usage, abort-result reporting.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — full-suite gate (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81),
  resume documentation/behaviour.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `query_cached` consumer; must still reject partial/abort
  entries as full-suite evidence.
- `tests/` — coverage for abort-vs-green preservation in this repo's test suite.
- Cross-repo (TCE, tracked here): `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout / § Test Configuration —
  document the resume path for TCE release operators.

## Related work

- **Sibling item: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit bound** (created alongside
  this one) — prevents the abort in the first place; this item makes the residual abort cheap to
  recover from. These are complementary, not sequential.
- **CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09** (TCE, superseded/deleted) — original intake; the abort cache entry is
  `.worklog/cache/3b6572d09f1a6363f3a1be3d020af939` (TCE), `exit_code: 124`, facts
  `elapsed=311.09s, configured_timeout=1500s`.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** (this repo) — the full-suite-at-dev-push gate that the release gate
  mirrors (cached runner makes repeat verification cheap).
- **WL-0MVPO9P610055UQ3** and `test_cache.py` pre-run/post-run keying history — the cache-state
  semantics this item must preserve.
- TCE CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N (browser-stage hang bound) and CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H (coverage gate) —
  the fail-closed invariants that must not regress.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q2 (resume-path scope: A docs only / B split into a framework item / C in-item framework
  edit) — ANSWERED: B (framework item; this item is that split).** Asked 2026-11-13 by Map in
  intake on CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09; answered by producer (comment): "2. B". Agent recommendation
  (adopted): the cache and gate are framework-owned here (`test_cache.py`,
  `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`), so the
  implementation lands in this repo and every project's release gate benefits from the fix;
  TCE-side documentation is cross-repo work recorded on this item.
- **Q1 (bound strategy) — ANSWERED separately** (C, hybrid): tracked in the sibling item; the
  diagnostic content it adds is what makes the abort entry's context readable here.
- **Duplicate check** — no existing item preserves green cache entries across abort results;
  `test_cache.py` writes the returned verdict unconditionally on the post-run state today (TCE
  `run_cached` usage observed via the 124 entry at 3b6572d09f…).
