# `implement.py start` must not fork a worktree from a local parent branch that is behind `origin/<parent>`

Mirror of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MWFF40700014EE2** (`discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2`).
Per the precedent producer decision for **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 ← AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB**
(2026-09-25: "the fix and regression tests live in the SorraAgents counterpart; no
implementation change is required in AI_Hell"), the actionable fix lives here, where
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` is.

## Problem

`implement.py start` refreshes the local parent branch before `git worktree add`, but
`_sync_parent_branch` **skips** the refresh when the local `dev` ref is diverged or cannot
be fetched non-checked-out (`reason: "diverged_or_checked_out"`), and `phase_start` then
forks the worktree from that stale local `dev` anyway (`git_worktree_add(branch,
abs_wt_path, parent_branch)` → `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <wt> dev`). The child
session inherits a base missing commits already published on `origin/dev`.

Observed during AH-0MWF0CS4I001XZHU (driven child of AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55):

- the main checkout's `dev` was `ahead 1, behind 8` of `origin/dev` (`e38797b8` local-only,
  duplicating `9687a6db`'s content);
- the worktree forked at `e38797b8`, so its changed-scope test gate ran an unrelated
  `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` against pre-fix source and went **red** on a failure
  `origin/dev` had already fixed (`HANGAR_WAR_SCENE_KEYS` still listing the deleted
  `DefenceReportScene`);
- the session had to rebase onto `origin/dev` (`8d1c1aca`) by hand before it could pass its
  gate and push.

The same symptom is recorded in AH-0MWEYVRUX008SLJ8's completion comments ("Push to dev
initially failed (non-fast-forward …). Rebased onto origin/dev and retried"), so this is
recurring, not a one-off.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree forked by `start` is based on a ref whose commits are all contained in
`origin/<parent>` (a fast-forward ancestor of `origin/<parent>`), so a driven child never
starts behind the published base.

## Approach (decided)

The AI_Hell report listed two candidate approaches ("fork from `origin/<parent>`" or
"warn loudly"); the acceptance criteria pin the first and make the second mandatory
reporting, so both are in scope:

1. `_sync_parent_branch` reports `ahead`/`behind` counts (via
   `git rev-list --left-right --count <local>...refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`) on every
   skip reason where the counts are computable, in addition to `reason`/`warning`.
2. A new resolver decides the fork base: **fork from
   `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` whenever the local parent is behind `origin/<parent>`
   (`behind > 0`, which includes the diverged case); otherwise keep the current local-branch
   base.** The local ref is never force-updated — a diverged local `dev` stays exactly as it
   is for the operator to reconcile.
3. `phase_start` records the choice: `report["steps"]["worktree_base"] = {ref, reason,
   ahead, behind}` and an extended "Implementation started"/"resumed" comment naming the base
   ref and, when the local branch was skipped, why plus the ahead/behind counts.
4. Fail-open is preserved: a held main-checkout lock, a failed fetch, or a dirty main checkout
   never blocks `start`; when the counts cannot be computed (fetch failed / no remote-tracking
   ref) the local branch remains the base exactly as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `implement.py start` never forks a worktree from a local parent branch that is
  behind `origin/<parent>`: either the local ref is fast-forwarded or the worktree is forked
  from `origin/<parent>`.
- **AC2** — The start report/comment names the base ref used and, when the local parent branch
  was skipped (diverged / checked out / lock held), states why and the ahead/behind counts.
- **AC3** — A driven child started from a diverged local `dev` passes its first changed-scope
  gate without a manual rebase (regression test with a synthetic diverged local branch).
- **AC4** — Existing behaviour is preserved: a lock-held or fetch-failed refresh still fails
  open (never blocks `start`) and never force-updates a diverged branch.

## Implementation sketch

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `_sync_parent_branch` (~line 7456): add `ahead`/`behind` to the skipped results
    (`diverged`, `diverged_or_checked_out`, and the other safe-skip paths where computable).
  - New `_resolve_worktree_base_ref(repo_root, parent_branch, refresh_result) -> dict`:
    returns `{"ref", "reason", "ahead", "behind", "skipped_local"}`; picks
    `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` when behind > 0.
  - `phase_start` Step 7 (~line 11370): pass the resolved ref to `git_worktree_add`, record
    `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]`, and name it in the start/resume comment (~line 11431).
  - `git_worktree_add` (~line 3435): document that the base may be a fully-qualified
    remote-tracking ref; assert the new branch still tracks `origin/<parent>` (the
    `--track` upstream must not change — `finish` pushes to `origin/dev`).
- Tests (test-first, new file `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py`, following
  the hermetic-fixture patterns in `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py` /
  `test_phase_start_claim.py`).
- Docs: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (start section ~2204-2216, ~4029) and
  `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (~357) — document the base-ref resolution and the new report
  keys/skip reasons.

## Related work

- `discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2` (AI_Hell discovery report; counterpart of this item)
- SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 (completed) — `finish` now fast-forwards local `dev` after the push;
  that closes the *common* stale-local-dev case, leaving the diverged/lock-held skip this
  item fixes.
- SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO — main-checkout lock shared by `start`'s refresh and `finish`.
- SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF — `start` resume-from-worktree path resolved against the main checkout.
- SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5 — behind-only child worktree detection (same "stale base" family).

## Impact

Driven child sessions start from the published base, so they stop burning a rebase and a red
gate on work someone else already shipped.

# Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6)

## Problem statement

Implement sessions that run concurrently spend the overwhelming majority of their
wall-clock waiting on a single per-repository `flock`, because `implement.py finish`
holds that lock across its **whole** commit → fast-forward → push → post-push window
and the dev-push **pre-push hook runs the full test suite (~5.4 min)** inside it.
Every concurrent `finish` therefore serialises its expensive test run behind the
others. At the intended fan-out of **up to 6 concurrent sessions**, the sixth finish
queues behind five ~5-min full-suite runs.

## Evidence (2026-11-13, AI_Hell implement-skill sessions)

Analysed the 36 worktree sessions that started with the implement skill
(`~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell-.worklog-*`):

- **668 min** summed session time over a **388 min (6.5 h)** wall-clock span —
  only **1.7x effective parallelism** at a **peak measured concurrency of 4**.
- **88–93%** of each long session's wall-clock was inside `bash` tool calls
  (waiting on processes), not model reasoning or edits.
- Time buckets: **wait_for_job 249 min (37%)** (215.9 min of it lock-waits),
  own `finish` 133 min (20%), scoped tests 57 min (9%), hand-rolled
  `sleep`/`grep` polling loops 48 min (7%).
- **57** "another run holds the repository lock" refusals; **46** observed
  lock-waits averaging **4.3 min** (median 5 min, **max 21.5 min**). Worst single
  tool call: **45 min** = a `for attempt in 1..8` retry loop absorbing five
  consecutive lock holders.
- **21** non-fast-forward rebase events, each creating a new tree that re-triggers
  the full-suite pre-push gate (9 full-suite gate runs today).
- 9 sessions were **no-ops** (3 messages, ~50 s) — drive retries that immediately
  gave up.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions
  (the intended operating point) on a single repository.
- **Implement-skill sessions** (leaf and driven child) whose `finish` currently queues
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs.
- **Producers/reviewers** who need the speed-up evidenced, not asserted.

User stories:

- As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
  complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised queueing
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in roughly the
  time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.
- As a driven child session, I want my single `finish` call to wait boundedly on the
  lock instead of scripting retry loops.
- As a producer, I want a recorded before/after measurement before the epic is closed.

## Goal

As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised
queueing behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in
roughly the time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.

## Decomposition

The epic is decomposed into five child items; together they own every acceptance
criterion below.

1. Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock
   (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the single biggest time sink: stop holding the exclusive
   repository lock across the ~5.4 min full-suite gate.
2. Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops
   (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF) — replace fail-fast refusals plus agent-scripted retry loops
   with one bounded internal wait that reports the holder.
3. Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC) — a lost
   push race currently pays the full suite again because the rebase produces a new tree.
4. Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up
   (SA-0MWFJSCPT005BO2R) — 9 of 36 sessions did no work.
5. Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out and record before/after analysis
   (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) — verifies the outcome ACs against real session logs; blocked
   by items 1–4.

## Acceptance criteria

- Under a 6-way concurrent `finish` fan-out, no session spends the majority of its
  wall-clock blocked on the per-repository lock (measured: median lock-wait per session < 60 s; no single lock-wait > 5 min).
- The full test suite is never executed while a single global repository lock is held (proved by inspection + test).
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A concrete before/after measurement is recorded (same 36-session style analysis).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Safety invariants stay intact: single-owner mutation of the shared `dev` ref, the
  bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and tree/provenance binding of gate verdicts
  (no verdict about a different tree/diff may be trusted).
- The dev-push gate keeps `scope=full` for release-critical refs — the speed-up must not
  weaken the release gate.
- Target concurrency is **up to 6**; designs are evaluated at that fan-out.

## Existing state

- `implement.py finish` acquires `<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`
  (`shared.repo_lock.RepoLock`) at Step 3c and holds it through push and post-push
  verification; `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast).
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --gate-commit <sha>` for
  pushes to `dev`/`main`, with a tree-keyed verdict cache (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`)
  and gate provenance lines, all of which execute inside the held finish lock today.
- Pushes to the shared `dev` ref lose the non-fast-forward race under concurrency; the
  rebase-and-retry path in `implement.py` produces a new tree and therefore a cache miss.
- `phase_drive` spawns one session per child; some spawns observe state that makes the
  child immediately terminal/blocked and exit as no-ops.

## Desired change

Concurrent `finish` runs overlap their expensive work instead of serialising on one
repository-wide critical section, and the epic's outcome is evidenced by a recorded
before/after session analysis.

## Impact

An operator can run a 6-way concurrent implement fan-out and have the batch finish in
roughly the time of one work item, instead of waiting for six serialised five-minute
test runs — while still shipping only fully tested commits.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 3c lock window, push/rebase retry path, `phase_drive` spawn decisions
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock` / bounded wait for `main-checkout.lock`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite gate, `test` semaphore lane, tree-keyed verdict cache
- `.githooks/pre-push` — dev/main full-suite gate and cache mirroring
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish/wait guidance to update
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py`, `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — existing regression coverage to extend

## Related work

- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper this epic shrinks the critical section of.
- implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward (SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) — established the single-owner lock invariant.
- Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans (SA-0MVPZG01J0067PC2) — concurrency test patterns to reuse.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the full suite sits at the gate.
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache that makes verdict reuse possible.
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — this epic's measurement items should reuse/feed it.
- Post-fix slot-wait re-measurement (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) — precedent methodology for before/after measurement.
- Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs (SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5) — push-race prior art.

## Out of scope

- Trimming the full suite's own runtime / sharding / per-file caching, and raising
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` — those are per-project (AI_Hell) concerns, not framework.
- Changing changed-scope test selection.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** moving the suite out of the lock could let an untested tree reach `dev`;
  mitigation is the tree/provenance-bound verdict and the ancestry assertion, both
  preserved by the owning children.
- **Risk:** verdict reuse after a rebase could accept a genuinely different diff;
  mitigated by provable content equality plus a negative test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general lock/push queue service is out of scope;
  the children take the smallest change that meets their ACs.
- **Assumption:** the measured symptom is lock serialisation, not per-project suite
  runtime — the baseline bucket analysis supports this (37% in `wait_for_job`, 215.9 min
  of it lock-waits).
- **Assumption:** sessions of comparable work-item size are available for the "after"
  measurement; otherwise a synthetic 6-way fan-out supplies it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What concurrency target must the design satisfy?" — Answer (operator, 2026-11-13):
  "Up to 6 concurrent implement sessions." Source: analysis comment on this item

# Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1). This is the single biggest time sink identified in the
2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` acquires the per-repository `flock`
(`<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`) at Step 3c and holds it until
the `finally` block — covering commit → fast-forward local dev → **push** → post-push
verification. The dev push triggers `.githooks/pre-push`, which runs the **full test
suite** (`run_tests.py --scope full`, measured ~326 s / 5.4 min for AI_Hell) while the
lock is held. A read-only test run is therefore made part of the exclusive mutating
critical section, so every concurrent `finish` serialises its ~5-min suite behind the
others. This is the root cause of the 37% `wait_for_job` share and the 46 lock-waits
(median 5 min, max 21.5 min).

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions.
- **Implement-skill session** whose `finish` currently spends most of its wall-clock
  waiting for the lock rather than doing work.

User stories:

- As an operator running a 6-way fan-out, I want concurrent finishes to overlap their
  full-suite gate runs so the batch finishes in roughly the time of one work item
  rather than the sum of all of them.
- As an implement-skill session, I want the exclusive repository lock to cover only
  the short mutating window, so my `finish` is not blocked for another session's
  ~5-minute test run.

## Goal

As an operator running concurrent implement sessions, I want the full-suite gate to
run **without** holding the exclusive repository lock, so concurrent finishes overlap
their test time instead of queueing on it.

## Approach

- Resolve the full-suite verdict for the *pushed tree* **before** taking the
  main-checkout lock (the tree-keyed cache already exists — reuse it), or run the
  suite under only the shared `test` semaphore lane, not the repo lock.
- Keep the lock covering only the true mutations: commit → fast-forward → push →
  ancestry assertion (should be seconds).
- Preserve the existing safety invariants: single-owner mutation of the shared `dev`
  ref, the bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and the tree/provenance binding of
  the verdict (no verdict about a different tree may be trusted).

## Acceptance criteria

- The full test suite is never executed while `main-checkout.lock` is held (asserted
  by a test that observes lock state across the suite invocation).
- The lock-hold window in a green `finish` is bounded and does not include the
  full-suite duration (measured/asserted in a test or documented metric).
- A concurrent-finish integration test shows the second finish's wait is materially
  shorter when the first is running the full suite (no longer serialised on suite
  time).
- No regression in the existing finish-concurrency / ancestry-assertion tests.
- At least one automated test proves the new gate/lock ordering (lock state observed
  while the suite runs, and a green finish whose lock window excludes the suite).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The shared `dev` ref stays single-owner: exactly one finish mutates it at a time and
  the ancestry assertion after the push is unchanged.
- The gate verdict remains provenance-bound and tree-keyed (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV,
  SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB): no verdict about a different tree may be reused, and a
  rebased commit legitimately produces a new tree (see the sibling rebase item).
- The bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` behaviour is preserved — no unbounded
  lock hold.
- Out of scope: trimming the full suite's own runtime, sharding, per-file caching,
  raising `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (per-project concerns), and changing changed-scope
  test selection.

## Existing state

- `phase_finish` acquires `main-checkout.lock` at Step 3c and holds it through push
  and post-push verification.
- `.githooks/pre-push` always runs `run_tests.py --scope full` for pushes to
  `dev`/`main` (scope-aware gate, SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61) and is bound to the pushed
  commit (`--gate-commit`), with a tree-keyed verdict cache and cache mirroring into
  the main checkout.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` already allocates an independent `test` semaphore
  lane and caches verdicts with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`.

## Desired change

The expensive read-only suite runs outside the exclusive repository lock (either
before acquiring it, keyed on the would-be pushed tree, or under the `test` lane
only), and the lock window shrinks to the commit → fast-forward → push → ancestry
assertion sequence.

## Impact

Concurrent finishes stop serialising behind each other's full-suite runs, so an
operator's 6-way fan-out batch completes in roughly the time of a single work item
instead of queueing six ~5-minute suites one after another.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 3c lock acquisition and the push/gate window (search `Step 3c`, `acquire_main_checkout_lock`)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite gate entry point, `test` semaphore lane, tree-keyed verdict cache (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`)
- `.githooks/pre-push` — dev/main full-suite gate that today runs inside the lock window
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock` / `release_repo_lock` implementing `main-checkout.lock`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` — existing lock-window tests to extend
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish lock/timeout documentation to update

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — lock helper reused here.
- implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward (SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) — establishes the single-owner lock invariant.
- Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans (SA-0MVPZG01J0067PC2) — test patterns to reuse.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the full suite is at the gate at all.
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache this item must reuse.
- Sibling items: Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF); Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC).
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — feeds the epic-level before/after measurement.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** making the suite asynchronous (background gate) would weaken
  the "never push an unverified tree" guarantee — out of scope; the verdict must still
  gate the push.
- **Risk:** moving the suite before the lock could test a tree that is then invalidated
  by a rebase; mitigations: reuse the tree-keyed verdict, and treat a rebase-produced
  tree as a cache miss (handled by the sibling rebase item).
- **Assumption:** the `dev` push gate stays `scope=full` for release-critical refs.
- **Assumption:** the suite's own runtime is a per-project concern; only the serialising
  effect is addressed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence base: the
2026-11-13 AI_Hell 36-session analysis recorded on the parent epic
(SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1 comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR), plus operator decisions recorded
there (concurrency target up to 6; per-project full-suite trimming out of scope).
Researched directly in the repository: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
(Step 3c lock window), `.githooks/pre-push` (full-suite gate), and
`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (tree-keyed verdict cache).

# Race-clobber restore regression tests

Parent: SA-0MW7Z77KI005MK0B (audit restore lost-update). Test-first slice: land
the regression suite for the concurrent-`wl sync` clobber **before** the fixes
(F2/F3), so each fix is proven by a red-then-green test.

## Scope

Deterministic clobber injection for the audit lifecycle restore paths: an
injectable `wl` runner/store that reverts an item to a stale
`open`/`plan_complete` snapshot at a scripted point (before the next `wl show`
readback, or after a verified readback), modelling the concurrent `wl sync`
lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ class).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` between the audit status change and its restore and asserts the item ends `completed`/`in_review`.
- [ ] A regression test injects a concurrent `wl sync` after the first verified restore readback and asserts the settle re-verification restores the item again.
- [ ] An aborted audit restores the item to `completed`/`in_review`, verified after write and retried once if a concurrent `wl sync` clobbered the restore, even when the clobber lands on the first restore write.
- [ ] A regression test raises an exception after the `in_progress` claim (audit lease / checkpoint store) and asserts the captured pre-audit state is restored, never `in_progress`.
- [ ] A JS unit test drives `checkAndRestoreStuckAudit` with a clobbered restore, asserts one bounded retry, and asserts the state file is retained when the restore cannot be verified.
- [ ] The harness (injectable runner recording every `wl update`/`wl show`, with scripted clobber points (a) before the first readback and (b) after a verified readback) lives in `skill/audit/tests/`; the suite is red pre-fix (red run recorded in a work-item comment) and green after the fixes; no duplication of existing `test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` coverage.

## Key Files:

- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_restore_race.py`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py`
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
- `tests/unit/test-check-audit-gate.mjs`
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`

## Out of scope

Fixing the restore paths (children F2/F3); fixing the general `wl sync`
lost-update race (WL-0MUXA5RI2009EUTJ).
